info.title: TravelDesk Agent API
info.description:
TravelDesk Agent (Reseller) API.

## Rate limiting

The quota is applied **per Agent Branch key** — the per-branch client id/secret pair — not per account, per host, or per integration. Standard branches get **200 calls per minute**; upgraded branches get **900**. That budget is shared across everything the branch does: availability refreshes, background sweeps, customer-facing pricing, and quote or booking creation.

Two consequences worth designing around:

- A background sweep can starve customer-facing traffic for the same branch. Give live requests priority over refresh work, and cap the concurrency of any bulk job.
- Cooldowns after a `429` must be keyed per branch. Keying them by host throttles every branch at once, because they all share `tdms.websitetravel.com`.

Prefer endpoints that answer for a whole product in one request — `/apiv1/checkAvailabilityProduct` over one `/apiv1/checkavailabilityrange` call per fareprice — since the saving is measured against this quota.

## Dates

Most endpoints take and return `DD-MON-YYYY` (`29-JUL-2026`). `/apiv1/checkAvailabilityProduct` returns ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` keys in `dates`. Parse both.

## Pricing

Accommodation is dynamically priced — rates move between individual dates, not just between seasons — so never cache one rate per fareprice and reuse it across a range. Nett tracks RRP at a fixed commission ratio per fareprice, because changing commission requires a new `productPricesDetailsId`; that makes nett safe to derive from RRP rather than store.

get.description:
Return booking details for a fareprice, including the list of custom booking fields (`optionalFields`) that must be collected from the customer before ordering.

Each `optionalFields` entry contains:

- `optionalFieldId` — integer or string ID to echo back on the order
- `title` / `commonName` — display label for the customer-facing form
- `type` — `text`, `select`, and similar
- `mandatory` — whether the customer must answer
- `options` — allowed values (for `select` types)

Submit the customer's answers on [`POST /apiv1/order`](#post-apiv1order) under `redeemer.products.bookings.optionalFields` as `{ optionalFieldId, fieldText }`. The value key **must** be `fieldText` — other names (e.g. `fieldValue`, `optionalFieldValue`) are silently dropped by TDMS.

get.summary: Check cached availability for every fareprice of a product
get.description:
Return cached availability and pricing for **all** fareprices of a product in one call, for a window starting at `from`.

Use this instead of calling `/apiv1/checkavailabilityrange/{productPricesDetailsId}/...` once per fareprice: a product with six fares costs one request here rather than six, which matters because the rate limit is applied per Agent Branch key.

The response is served from the availability cache, so it is fast but not live. Confirm price and availability with a live call before you take payment.

Not every product supports this endpoint. When it does not, the request fails with `400` and a `not_supported` message — fall back to `/apiv1/checkavailabilityrange` per fareprice.

Example: `GET /apiv1/checkAvailabilityProduct?productId=9027&from=29-JUL-2026&days=90`

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: The Product ID to check. Every fareprice of the product is returned.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first date to check, in `DD-MON-YYYY` format — for example `29-JUL-2026`.

parameters.name: days
parameters.description: The number of days to check, including the start date. Walk longer ranges in successive requests.

200.description:
Product metadata plus availability and pricing for every fareprice, keyed by date.

`dates` maps each date to an **array**, because a fareprice can run at several booking times on the same day. Each entry carries its own `numAvailable`, `rrp`, `bookingTimeId` and pickup list. If you are selling a single departure, choose one entry — do not sum them.

Two prices are returned. `fares[].rrp` is the fareprice's standing rate; `fares[].dates[...][].rrp` is the rate for that date. **Use the per-date figure.** Accommodation in particular is repriced between individual dates, so the standing rate is only a fallback for a date the cache has no row for.

Field casing differs from `/apiv1/checkavailabilityrange`, which returns `NumAvailable` and nests its price under `productPricingData.RRP`. Reading the wrong one fails silently — counts populate while the price stays null, which looks like an unpriced fare rather than a parse error.

**Responses can be large.** `additionalFields` embeds every option of every select, including full country lists, repeated per date entry. A 30-day window on a product with several fares can run to megabytes, so read the fields you need and discard the rest rather than holding the whole payload.

image.description: Absolute URL to the product image.

productPricesDetailsId.description: The Product Prices Detail ID of the fareprice.

rrp.description: The fareprice's standing rate. Prefer the per-date `rrp` below.

hasAvailability.description: False when the fareprice has no availability anywhere in the window. Use it to skip a fare without walking its dates.

dates.description: Keyed by ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Each value is an array of one entry per booking time.

bookingTimeId.description: The identifier to send when booking, for example `13_00_00`. A product with a single daily departure returns `0`.

numAvailable.description: Places remaining for this fareprice at this booking time.

rrp.description: Retail price per person for this date. Prefer this over the fareprice's standing rate.

pickupLocations.description: Pickup points offered on this departure. Required at booking where the product uses them.

additionalFields.description: Passenger details this departure requires at booking. Read this rather than hard-coding a form: the set varies by product, and `required` varies with it.

options.description: Present for `select`. Can be very long — `Nationality` returns the full country list on every date entry.

supplier.name: Australian Adventure Group Holdings Pty Ltd

400.description: The product does not support cached availability. The message contains `not_supported`. Fall back to `/apiv1/checkavailabilityrange` per fareprice.

403.description: Not authorised.

404.description: Product not found, or not available to this agent. Also returned once you walk past the end of the product's bookable dates, so treat a `404` that follows at least one successful window as the end of the calendar rather than a failure.

500.description: **Also returned for a window that simply has no results**, with the message `Unable to fetch cached availability`. This is a known defect, confirmed in Postman and raised with the TravelDesk developers on 2026-07-27. Treat that specific message as an empty window and keep walking — a seasonal product can have an empty 90-day span followed by a full one, so stopping here silently drops every later departure.

post.description:
Submit an order with products, customers, and booking details.

## Custom booking fields (optionalFields)

Many products define custom booking fields the supplier needs at check-in — driver note, mobile number, flight number, accommodation, dietary requirements, age, and similar. Discover the fields for a fareprice via [`GET /apiv1/bookingdetails/{productPricesDetailsId}`](#get-apiv1bookingdetails-productpricesdetailsid); each entry returns an `optionalFieldId`, `title`, `type`, and `mandatory` flag.

Submit the customer's answers on `redeemer.products.bookings.optionalFields` as `{ optionalFieldId, fieldText }`:

```json
"optionalFields": [
  { "optionalFieldId": 811109, "fieldText": "2:35" },
  { "optionalFieldId": "MobilePhone", "fieldText": "0412 000 000" }
]
```

> **The value key must be `fieldText`.** TDMS silently ignores unknown keys such as `fieldValue` or `optionalFieldValue` — the order still succeeds, but the booking arrives at the supplier with an empty `additionalFields` array and the operator never sees the customer's answer. If a booking is reaching the supplier with no custom field data, inspect the outbound payload and confirm the key name first.
